title: Trace-driven tail sampler and burn-fencing policy for precision paging
creator: Jonah Liu
description:
Problem: We are receiving a large volume of noisy burn-rate and latency pages that are not actionable for oncall. Existing burn-rate alerts trigger on aggregated SLI deviations without contextual trace fingerprints, and our current sampling drops many of the tail traces needed to root-cause transient bursts. This increases MTTR and leads to fatigue.

Goal: Reduce noisy pages while preserving or improving detection of real SLO violations by: (1) implementing a trace-driven tail sampler that preferentially retains traces associated with high-latency/error slices and rare request fingerprints, (2) enriching burn-rate alerts with an "anomaly confidence" signal derived from trace embeddings and recent signature uniqueness, and (3) introducing a burn-fencing policy that suppresses pagering for alerts with low root-cause confidence but surfaces them to duty dashboards and a low-priority notification channel.

Scope: Changes span tracing hooks (sampling decision enrichment), metrics/log pipeline sampling config, alert enrichment logic (confidence scoring), Console dashboard updates (duty and escalation lanes), and rollout controls (feature flag + gradual ramp). This ticket covers design, prototype, and initial canary in prod for a single platform team (model-serving). Full rollouts for other teams will be follow-ups.
updates: 2026-02-12: Initial spike completed. Benchmarked trace volume vs tokenized request fingerprints on model-serving; tail traces constitute ~4.8% of request volume but contain 72% of post-failure stack attachments.

2026-02-18: Design doc reviewed with Observability and Oncall leads. Decided on hybrid sampling: deterministic retention for traces with latency > 200ms or any 5xx, plus probabilistic retention upweighted by rarity score (inverse frequency of request fingerprint).

2026-02-22: Tracing hook prototype implemented in tracing-sidecar. Sampling decision now includes retention_reason tag and fingerprint hash. Local end-to-end tests pass. PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/telemetry/pull/612

2026-02-25: Pipeline change sketched: telemetry-ingest will accept sampler hints as headers and persist sampled raw traces to long-term trace-backstore for 7 days. Ingest team suggested batching hints to avoid overheads.

2026-02-27: Alert enrichment model trained on two months of historical traces and SLI events. Model outputs a 0-100 confidence score combining: trace-embedding distance to prior failures, fingerprint rarity, and recent SLO momentum. Initial offline validation shows precision improvement for actionable pages from 0.46 -> 0.71.

2026-03-01: Canary plan drafted. Feature flag trace_tail_sampler.v1 created. Canary target: model-serving prod cluster in us-west-2, 10% traffic, 72h evaluation window. Dashboard template created: TraceTailSampler Canary (Console link placeholder: https://console.redwood/test/trace-tail-canary).
acceptance_criteria: Canary telemetry shows >= 30% reduction in actionable P1 pages for model-serving without increasing missed SLO violations by more than 5% (measured over 72h window)
Trace-sidecar annotates sampling decisions with retention_reason and fingerprint hash in 100% of sampled traces for the canary cluster
Alert enrichment confidence score attached to burn-rate alerts in Console and used by the paging policy
Burn-fencing policy implemented in Pager service: low-confidence alerts are routed to the duty dashboard + low-priority Slack channel instead of immediate pager
Dashboards and runbooks updated and linked from the alert UI; oncall training doc published
Performance overhead for tracing hooks < 1.5% p95 CPU and < 5ms added p95 latency on request path during canary
implementation_plan: Step 1: Merge tracing-sidecar prototype (PR #612) behind feature flag. Ensure robust unit tests for retention_reason annotation.
Step 2: Deploy ingest-side change to accept sampler hints and tag persisted traces. Add backfill capability to pull dropped traces if needed for RCA.
Step 3: Integrate enrichment model in Alerting service; expose confidence score in alert payload and Console UI lanes.
Step 4: Implement burn-fencing in Pager service with configurable thresholds and escalation lanes. Add 'quiet escalate' path for low-confidence but high-impact alerts.
Step 5: Run 72h canary on model-serving (10% traffic). Monitor precision/recall, MTTA, page volume, system overhead.
Step 6: Iterate model thresholds and rarity weighting based on canary metrics; prepare rollout plan for other teams.
Step 7: Post-mortem and launch notes; schedule follow-ups for storage retention policy and GA plan.
risks_and_mitigation: Risk: Sampling bias could miss correlated failures that manifest only in non-tail traces. Mitigation: keep deterministic retention for any 5xx and use periodic full-scan synthetic probes to validate coverage.

Risk: Confidence model overfits to historical signatures and suppresses novel failures. Mitigation: maintain an 'unknown anomaly' fallback that bypasses burn-fencing when SLO momentum is rapidly degrading and schedule weekly model retraining.
Risk: Storage and ingest cost increases. Mitigation: limit long-term retention to 7 days for sampled tail traces and purge older buckets; evaluate compression/quantization options.
Risk: Oncall unfamiliarity with new lanes. Mitigation: update runbooks, provide a 1-hour training session during canary, and include automated runbook links in alerts.
notes: This ticket intentionally targets only the tracing + alerting enrichment surface; complementary UX improvements for Console (compact RCA view) will be a separate PM/Design ticket.
Related investigations: ENG-51764 (chronicle probe enricher) and ENG-246901 (dashboard-driven incident scorer) provide useful telemetry features we can reuse.
If the canary metrics meet goals, propose expanding to deduped multi-service lanes and adding an SLO-shadowing mode for 30 days before full pager cutoff.
